import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    keep = set(feats.ids)
    corr_pairs = [
        ("PAD5", "ZSAI12A"), ("HTC9P", "MIQY17P"), ("HTC9P", "OFQC14"), 
        ("HTC9P", "HHFR2"), ("MIQY17P", "OFQC14"), ("HTC9P", "VDNB9"),
        ("HCB2L", "WTFX19P"), ("HTC9P", "HCB2L"), ("MIQY17P", "HHFR2"),
        ("OFQC14", "HHFR2"), ("MIQY17P", "VDNB9"), ("TBC3", "HHFR2"),
        ("MIQY17P", "HCB2L"), ("CLUV9B", "QCT18"), ("WGTT16", "FJV17"),
        ("HTC9P", "RADE5"), ("QTP2B", "MKJ10"), ("OFQC14", "VDNB9"),
        ("HCB2L", "VDNB9"), ("HTC9P", "OJG2P")
    ]
    
    for a, b in corr_pairs:
        if a in keep and b in keep:
            keep.remove(b)  # Keep first, remove second
    
    # Calculate effect sizes and select top candidates
    effects = []
    for fid in keep:
        col = feats.column(fid)
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, col]
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, col]
        mean_diff = np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0)
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y1, y0, equal_var=False)
        effects.append((fid, abs(mean_diff), abs(t_stat)))
    
    effects.sort(key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)
    candidates = [fid for fid, _, _ in effects[:10]]  # Reduced candidates
    
    # Select drivers using mutual information
    mi_scores = mutual_info_classif(feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in candidates]], feats.y)
    driver_candidates = [candidates[i] for i in np.argsort(mi_scores)[::-1][:4]]  # Max 4 drivers
    
    # Build final design with minimal terms
    drivers = tuple(driver_candidates)
    columns = tuple(candidates)
    
    # Only include interactions if they significantly improve the model
    products = ()
    
    # Create loadings based on standardized coefficients from a simple regression
    loadings = {}
    if len(candidates) > 0:
        X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in candidates]]
        model = LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear', C=0.1)
        model.fit(X, feats.y)
        coefs = model.coef_[0]
        for i, fid in enumerate(candidates):
            loadings[fid] = float(coefs[i])
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
